# dockercompose_network (Data Source)

Looks up an existing Docker network by name and exposes its attributes. Use this to reference a network that this Terraform config doesn't manage — created by another team, a bootstrap script, or `docker network create` run directly — instead of a [`dockercompose_network`](../resources/network.md) resource. The lookup fails at plan/apply time if the network doesn't exist.

The most common use is feeding the looked-up name into a [`dockercompose_stack`](../resources/stack.md)'s `network` block via `external_name`, so the stack joins the network without owning its lifecycle.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    dockercompose = {
      source  = "ritajhq/dockercompose"
      version = "~> 1.1"
    }
  }
}

data "dockercompose_network" "edge" {
  name = "edge"
}

resource "dockercompose_stack" "api" {
  name = "api-stack"

  service {
    name     = "api"
    image    = "myapp/api:latest"
    networks = ["edge"]
  }

  network {
    name          = "edge"
    external      = true
    external_name = data.dockercompose_network.edge.name
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Docker network name to look up.

### Read-Only

- `attachable` (Boolean) Whether containers can be manually attached.
- `driver` (String) Network driver (bridge, overlay, host, none).
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `internal` (Boolean) Whether the network restricts external access.
- `ipam_driver` (String) IPAM driver.
- `ipam_gateway` (String) IPAM gateway of the first configured pool (e.g. '172.28.0.1').
- `ipam_subnet` (String) IPAM subnet of the first configured pool (e.g. '172.28.0.0/16').
- `labels` (Map of String) Network labels.
- `scope` (String) Network scope (local, swarm).
